format: Animation tick conformance vectors. Core (renderer.scheduling.test.ts) and Rust (tests/animation.rs) run this file.
Each subscriber requests a frame in its tick, on a manual clock that steps 1 ms at a time, with frames at up to 60 per second.

A frame row is [name, rates, offsets, options, frames, ticks]: subscribers at rates (fps) mounted at offsets (ms) count frames and ticks per second over the 5 s after the first. Slower subscribers tick up to half an interval late, so close rates that never align share frames.

options: tolerance (ms) and early (timers fire 1 ms early) are Core only: Rust has no tolerance option and its timers fire on time. live adds a frame source at the frame rate cap: Core's requestLive, Rust's animate.
rust: Rust's [frames, ticks] where the frame rate cap decides them. Core's manual clock floors timer delays to whole ms, so its 60 fps cap paces frames 16 ms apart; Rust's paces them 1/60 s apart.

bound: trials of random rates, mount offsets and content frames from a Park-Miller generator; frames per second never exceed the fastest rate (at most 60) plus the content frames alone, and each subscriber gets its rate within 1 tick per second.
frames: issue 350: 20, 12.5 and 10 fps share the 20 fps frames
equal rates mounted apart tick together
tolerance 0 with timers that fire 1 ms early
above maxFps, ticks arrive as counts
